ADDICTION MEDICINE NOTE   Date: 2026-01-01
44F, emergency room encounter with follow-up in the outpatient program.

S:
Patient was seen in the emergency room and is reviewed here for continuity of her outpatient program care. She reports strong cravings over the past two weeks, worse in the late evening and when alone. She attends group twice weekly and individual counseling on Mondays but missed two sessions this month due to fatigue. She works as a laundry attendant. Symptoms limit her to about 2 hours of activity before she needs to rest; she missed 6 shifts last month. Denies chest pain. Sleep is poor, around 5 hours. Appetite is fair. Lives with a roommate who supports her recovery.

O:
BP 122/78, HR 84, RR 14, Temp 98.5 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 149 lb, stable.
General: alert, cooperative, fatigued appearing.
HEENT: pupils equal and reactive.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Skin: no track marks or lesions.
Psych: linear thought process, fair insight, engaged in discussion of goals.
Labs (drawn in the ED): comprehensive metabolic panel within normal limits, urine drug screen reviewed with patient.

A/P:
1. Psychoactive substance dependence, active, engaged in outpatient treatment. Continue group and individual counseling and current medication-assisted treatment. Reviewed a relapse-prevention plan and evening coping strategies. Provided program crisis line information and confirmed the next appointment.
2. Supportive care: discussed sleep hygiene and pacing of daily tasks to manage fatigue. Coordinated with the case manager on transportation so she can attend all sessions.
3. Function and work: reduced activity tolerance is affecting her ability to keep shifts. Discussed documentation to support a gradual return to a regular schedule.

Return to the program in 1 week, sooner if cravings escalate or she feels unsafe.
